name: Ari Emanuel
evidence: Agency employment predates co-founding Endeavor. Informal childhood lawn-mowing is not a separate identifiable company in this classification.

name: Jeremy Stern
evidence: Guest is Colossus editor-in-chief. No commercial founder role established in this research; do not confuse him with Colossus founder Patrick O'Shaughnessy.

name: Alexander Taubman
evidence: Describes starting his career at Goldman and then building investment and operating businesses.

name: Ronnie Fieg
employment: David Z stock boy, salesperson and buyer
evidence: Started at David Z at 13 and worked there for approximately 15 years before Kith.

name: Peter Rahal
employment: Fruit-processing internships, including a placement in Belgium
evidence: First-person How I Built This interview describes working in Belgium after graduation, before returning home and starting RXBAR. Not counted merely because his family owned a food business. Founding-year reporting varies between 2012 and 2013; sequence is consistent.

name: Luca Ferrari
evidence: McKinsey overlaps work on Evertale, so it cannot simply be treated as a job before becoming a founder. It clearly predates Bending Spoons.

name: Mati Staniszewski
evidence: Official employer biography explicitly places Palantir before ElevenLabs. Student-led Mathscon is not treated as a commercial company.

name: Zach Dell
evidence: Finance employment predates Base Power, but he had already founded Thread in high school. No earlier employment sequence established.

name: Doug Leone
evidence: Founder of Sequoia was Don Valentine. Current episode describes Leone returning to Sequoia, not founding a new company at 69. No commercial founder role established here.

name: Torsten Reil
evidence: Oxford identifies him as a DPhil student when NaturalMotion emerged. Academic research is not automatically employment at someone else's company. Later employment/ownership is not sufficiently separated here.

name: Sam Altman
evidence: Loopt began while leaving Stanford. A Goldman internship offer was reportedly not taken. An offer, investing and YC leadership after founding Loopt do not establish employment before his first founding.

name: Travis Kalanick
evidence: Cutco sales precede Uber, but available summaries disagree on dates relative to his teenage SAT-prep business. Conservative first-company classification stays unclear.

name: Lulu Cheng Meservey
employment: J.P. Morgan financial analyst; World Bank consultant; McLarty adviser
evidence: TrailRunner's own biography in its FARA registration lists these earlier roles. Substack/Activision alone would only establish employment before her later company Rostra.

name: Michael Ovitz
employment: Fox while in college; William Morris trainee and agent
evidence: Describes full-time Fox work while at UCLA; William Morris employment also precedes founding CAA.

name: Micky Malka
evidence: SEC biography establishes co-founding Heptagon at 18. No preceding employee/intern role established. Later investing or CEO roles in his own companies do not qualify.

name: David Heinemeier Hansson
firstKnownBusiness: Early web projects / Basecamp founder-partner role
evidence: Freelance work, early web ventures and joining an existing 37signals partnership need a clearer chronology. Partnership entry is not automatically founding the existing company.

name: Jeff Zalaznick
firstKnownBusiness: Restaurant websites before Major Food Group
employment: J.P. Morgan analyst; Mandarin Oriental employee
evidence: Explicit employee-to-entrepreneur chronology before his first restaurant websites, not just before MFG.

name: Eric Glyman
employment: Houlihan Lokey summer analyst; Millstein financial analyst
evidence: Contemporaneous professional biography and dated career history place finance work before Paribus. His student/nonprofit Global China Connection role is outside the commercial-company definition.

name: Jonathan Ross
evidence: Employer biography explicitly identifies Google work before founding Groq. Creating an internal chip project is not a separate company founding.

name: Scott Wu
evidence: Episode biography places employee work at Scale AI before co-founding Lunchclub. Founding engineer is an employee role, not assumed to mean company co-founder.

name: Steve Stoute
employment: Sony and Interscope executive; Arnell Group employee
evidence: Strong employment history before Translation, but earliest independent management business and childhood work chronology remain unresolved. Later employment is not proof of employee-first.

name: Ed Catmull
employment: NYIT researcher; Lucasfilm computer division head
evidence: Hired to Lucasfilm in 1979; the division was spun out as Pixar in 1986. An internal research group is not counted as his own commercial company.

name: Gustav Soderstrom
evidence: Yahoo employment followed his first company. Spotify is not his founding role. The episode summary calls him a 13th Lab co-founder while another biography calls him an adviser, so that later-founder claim is not used in the count.

name: Ivanka Trump
employment: Forest City Ratner project manager; Trump Organization employee
evidence: Employment before launching her own collection is established in contemporary interviews and the episode history.

name: Rick Rubin
evidence: Started Def Jam from his NYU dorm. No preceding employee role established; making music or recording his own band is not employment evidence.

name: Strauss Zelnick
employment: Columbia Pictures executive from 1983; later studio/music leadership
evidence: Episode biography explicitly places Columbia employment in 1983 and ZMC founding in 2001.

name: Dana White
evidence: Interviewed former colleague dates bellhop work to 1987, before the boxing business. White did not found the original UFC, which is not the founding anchor used here.

name: Adam Foroughi
evidence: Episode history places derivatives trading before his two earlier mobile-ad businesses, rather than treating AppLovin as his first founding.

name: David Baszucki
employment: General Motors engineering internship while at Stanford
evidence: GM placement during university predates 1985 graduation and subsequent Knowledge Revolution founding. This record uses a secondary biography and should be upgraded to a direct interview citation when available.

name: Evan Spiegel
employment: Red Bull and Abraxis BioScience internships in high school; Intuit internship
evidence: First-person episode transcript places high-school internships and Intuit before starting Future Freshman with Bobby Murphy, then Snapchat. Earlier company is included rather than treating Snapchat as the first founding.

name: Tony Xu
employment: Restaurant dishwasher as a child; later professional work
evidence: Episode history describes working alongside his mother at a restaurant well before DoorDash. Informal childhood ventures are not treated as separate identifiable companies.

name: Marc Andreessen
evidence: University Mosaic work and subsequent EIT employment precede Netscape. Mosaic as a university software project is not itself a company founding.

name: Brian Armstrong
firstKnownBusiness: Tutoring business in college, before Coinbase
employment: Airbnb engineer; possible college library work
evidence: Airbnb employment clearly predates Coinbase, but he had already run a tutoring business. The library-wage comparison in the transcript is insufficient to establish his own earlier employment chronology.

name: Jason Fried
evidence: First-person interview gives both first job at 13 and first self-owned entrepreneurial project at approximately 16.

name: Jimmy Iovine
evidence: Studio employment and engineering work predate his record-label founding. Work with an artist alone is not used as evidence of founding or mentorship.

name: Tobi Lutke
evidence: German apprenticeship predates moving to Canada in 2002 and Snowdevil in 2004. Count includes apprenticeships, not merely schooling.

name: John Mackey
employment: Busboy, dishwasher, camp counselor and Good Food store assistant manager
evidence: Directly lists pre-founder jobs and the Good Food experience that preceded his own store.

name: Patrick O'Shaughnessy
firstKnownBusiness: Invest Like the Best / Colossus; Positive Sum
evidence: Episode history places OSAM internship before his podcast and media/investment company founding. Employment in a family firm qualifies.

name: James Dyson
evidence: Official Dyson history explicitly contrasts salaried Rotork work with going independent in 1974.

name: Todd Graves
evidence: Official company history says these jobs funded the first restaurant.

name: Brad Jacobs
evidence: Sources establish first founding at 23, but not a prior employee role. Ludwig Jesselson mentorship is not assumed to be employment.

name: Michael Dell
employment: Restaurant dishwasher from age 12; stamp-store worker; newspaper salesperson
evidence: First-person interview establishes childhood jobs before PC's Limited. Ordering versus earliest childhood stamp-selling ventures is unresolved.

name: Daniel Ek
employment: Tradera and Stardoll roles before Spotify
evidence: Had already founded a web business before adult employment. Founding ages vary in sources, but neither supports employment before that first business.
